identity.author: John Davenant
identity.work: Two Dissertations (De praedestinatione through Cap. X Arg. V)
identity.edition: Dissertationes duae (Cambridge: Roger Daniel, 1650). Partial through Cap. X Arg. V (given to Christ / Augustine). Further Cap. X remains.

scope.locus: De praedestinatione Cap. X Arg. V given/not-given to Christ.
scope.next_locus: Cap. X Arg. VI+ (continue confirmation of non-election from mere will).

sections.title: Cap. X Arg. V: therefore election/predestination and preterition/reprobation do not hang on antecedent foresight of faith or unbelief — they precede such foresight
english: So election — that is, predestination — and preterition — that is, reprobation — do not hang on antecedent foresight of faith and perseverance in some, and of unbelief and pertinacity in others. They precede that foresight.
sections.latin: Electio sive praedestinatio, et praeteritio sive reprobatio non pendent ex praevisione antecedanea fidei et perseverantiae in quibusdam, ac infidelitatis et pertinaciae in aliis, sed talem praevisionem antecedunt.

sections.title: Cap. X Arg. V Major: John x. 28–29 — the Father gave Christ certain sheep no force can snatch; giving = electing singular persons to defend and lead infallibly to eternal life
english: The Major's truth is plain from these Scripture witnesses (John x. 28–29): No one snatches my sheep out of my hand. My Father, who gave them to me, is greater than all; and no one can snatch them out of my Father's hand. What sense have the words The Father gave Christ certain sheep that no force can snatch — unless this: God the Father, by electing, gave Christ certain singular persons, whom he decreed to defend against all assaults and snares of flesh, world, and devil, and at last to lead infallibly to the fruition of everlasting life?
sections.latin: Majoris veritas ex hisce Scripturarum testimoniis patet; Joann. x. 28, 29. Nemo rapit oves meas de manu mea. Pater meus, qui eas dedit mihi, major omnibus est: neque quisquam potest eas rapere e manu Patris mei. Quaero quis sensus horum verborum, Pater Christo dedit oves certas, quas nulla vis potest rapere, nisi, Deus Pater eligendo dedit Christo singulares quasdam personas, quas decrevit contra omnes carnis, mundi, et diaboli impetus insidiasque defendere, atque tandem ad fruitionem aeternae vitae infallibiliter perducere?

sections.title: Cap. X Arg. V Major: not to be given to Christ by the Father = not ordained by that gracious decree to obtain eternal life in and through Christ; John xvii. 9; Eph. i. 4–5
english: On the contrary: what is it not to be given to Christ by the Father, except this — not to be ordained by that gracious decree to obtain everlasting life infallibly in Christ and through Christ? Those words look the same way (John xvii. 9): I ask not for the world, but for those whom you have given me, because they are yours. So there are some not-given to Christ, not numbered in God the Father's peculiar flock — that is, non-elect before the world's foundations were laid, not predestined to the adoption of sons according to the benevolent affection of the divine will (Eph. i. 4–5, etc.).
sections.latin: E contra, quid est non dari Christo a Patre, nisi tali gratioso decreto ad vitam aeternam in Christo et per Christum infallibiliter obtinendam minime ordinari? Quo etiam spectant illa verba, Joann. xvii. 9. Non pro mundo rogo, sed pro iis quos dedisti mihi, quia tui sunt. Sunt igitur quidam non-dati Christo, non numerati in peculio Dei Patris, hoc est, non-electi antequam jacerentur mundi fundamenta, non-praedestinati in adoptionem filiorum pro benevolo affectu voluntatis Divinae, Eph. i. 4, 5, etc.

sections.title: Cap. X Arg. V Major: Augustine — those given to Christ are ordained to eternal life, predestined and called according to purpose, none of whom perish; given = elect; not-given = reprobate/passed over
english: Augustine always liked this reading of those words: These are understood as given to Christ who are ordained to everlasting life. They are the predestined, and called according to purpose, of whom none perishes (De corr. et grat. cap. 9). And in Tract. 106 on John's Gospel: Those whom God the Son elected from the world with the Father, the same as man the Son received from the world from the Father. For the Father would not have given them to the Son unless he had elected them. So you see: by those given to Christ, on Augustine's mind, nothing else is meant than the elect or predestined. And on the contrary, by the not-given the reprobate are meant — that is, the passed over and not predestined — which Augustine equally confesses.
sections.latin: Augustino haec praedictorum verborum semper placuit sententia: Hi Christo intelliguntur dari, qui ordinati sunt in vitam aeternam. Ipsi sunt illi praedestinati, et secundum propositum vocati, quorum nullus perit, De corr. et grat. cap. 9. Et in Evang. Joann. Tractat. 106. Quos Deus Filius de mundo elegit cum Patre, idem ipse homo Filius de mundo accepit a Patre. Non enim Pater illos Filio dedisset, nisi elegisset. Videtis igitur per datos Christo, ex mente Augustini, nil aliud intelligi, quam electos sive praedestinatos: Et e contra, per non-datos intelligi reprobatos, hoc est, praeteritos et minime praedestinatos, apud eundem Augustinum aeque in confesso est.

sections.title: Cap. X Arg. V Major: Augustine Tract. 107/111 — world = those not in the lot of grace to be chosen out of it; those not given are those to whom Christ will not give eternal life = the passed-over alone
english: Hence on Tract. 107 on John's Gospel, at the words I ask not for the world, but for these whom you have given me, he writes: By world he means those who live by the world's lust, and are not in that lot of grace to be chosen by him out of the world. And Tract. 111: They have not been given to him to whom he will not give everlasting life. But who finally are those to whom Christ will not give everlasting life, except those — and those alone — whom we call the passed over, non-elect or reprobate? For to all the elect he will give it.
sections.latin: Hinc Tract. 107. in Evang. Joann. ad haec verba, Non pro mundo rogo, sed pro his quos dedisti mihi, sic scribit; Mundum vult intelligi, qui vivunt secundum concupiscentiam mundi, et non sunt in ea sorte gratiae ut ab illo eligantur ex mundo. Et Tract. 111: Non ei dati sunt, quibus vitam non dabit aeternam. At quinam tandem illi sunt, quibus Christus non dabit vitam aeternam, nisi illi, et illi soli, quos appellamus praeteritos, non-electos sive reprobatos? nam omnibus electis dabit eam.

sections.title: Cap. X Arg. V Minor: given/not-given distinction precedes human faith and perseverance — John vi. 37: coming to Christ depends on the Father's giving as antecedent cause
english: Now to the Minor: let us show that this distinction of those given and not-given to Christ precedes human faith and perseverance, and also precedes absolute foresight of human unbelief and pertinacity. That it precedes faith and perseverance is gathered from these words: Whatever the Father gives me will come to me; and him who comes to me I will not cast out (John vi. 37). From those words it is plain: coming to Christ and remaining in Christ — that is, believing in Christ and persevering in faith — depends on this giving of the Father as on an antecedent cause.
sections.latin: Veniamus nunc ad Minorem, et ostendamus hanc distinctionem datorum et non-datorum Christo antecedere fidem et perseverantiam humanam, antecedere etiam praevisionem absolutam infidelitatis et pertinaciae humanae. Quod fidem et perseverantiam antecedat ex illis verbis colligitur, Quicquid mihi dat Pater, ad me veniet: et eum qui venit ad me non ejiciam foras, Joann. vi. 37. Manifestum est ex hisce verbis, venire ad Christum et permanere in Christo, quod est credere in Christum et in fide perseverare, ex hac datione Patris, tanquam ex antecedente causa dependere.

sections.title: Cap. X Arg. V Minor: John xvii. 6, 15, 24 and Matt. xiii. 11 — order: persons given to Christ first; then Spirit opens hearts to faith; then he sustains them; God does not elect from foresight of free-will faith
english: The same is plain in John xvii. 6, where Christ says he has manifested his Father's name to the men the Father gave him from the world. And verse 15: he asks specially for these, that they be kept from that evil one, and led to everlasting glory (verse 24). Matthew xiii. 11 serves the same point: To you it is given to know the mysteries of the kingdom of heaven; to them it is not given. In these places the order itself must be carefully watched. First, certain persons are given to Christ to be quickened and saved from God the Father's special good pleasure. Then Christ, by a special operation of his Spirit, opens their hearts so they conceive saving knowledge of God and faith. At last he so governs and sustains the illuminated and converted that no devil's temptations seduce them to ruin. God does not look to see who by free choice excited by grace will believe and persevere, and from that foresight elect them while passing others over. He elects some from his mere good pleasure, and gives them to Christ; Christ inspires faith in them that they may come to God, and implants perseverance that they may not withdraw from him.
sections.latin: Idem patet Joann. xvii. 6. Ubi Christus dicit se manifestasse nomen Patris sui hominibus, quos dedit illi de mundo. Et vers. 15. Rogat specialim pro hisce, ut serventur a malo illo, et ad gloriam aeternam perducantur vers. 24. Huc etiam faciunt illa verba Matth. xiii. 11. Vobis datum est nosse mysteria regni caelorum, illis non est datum. In quibus locis ipse ordo est diligenter observandus. Primo, certae quaedam personae dantur Christo vivificandae et salvandae ex speciali beneplacito Dei Patris. Tum Christus speciali operatione Spiritus sui aperit horum corda, ut salutiferam Dei cognitionem ac fidem concipiant. Tandem illuminatos et conversos ita gubernat et sustentat, ut nullis diaboli tentationibus ad interitum seducantur. Non ergo speculatur Deus quinam sunt libero suo arbitrio per gratiam excitato credituri et perseveraturi, et ex hac praevisione aliis praeteritis eos eligit, sed eligit quosdam ex mero suo beneplacito, donatque Christo, quibus Christus inspirat fidem ut accedant ad Deum, et indit perseverantiam ne recedant ab eo.

sections.title: Cap. X Arg. V Minor close: Augustine Tract. 105 — the Son is glorified so as to make the Father known to all given him; being given to Christ (that is, elected) is prior to knowing
english: Hear again the same Augustine: So he glorifies the Son, that to all whom you have given him he may make you known (Tract. 105. on John's Gospel). Therefore being given to Christ by the Father — that is, being elected — is prior to knowing.
sections.latin: Audiamus eundem quem antea audivimus Augustinum; Sic se Filium glorificat, ut omnibus quos dedisti ei te cognitum faciat, Tract. 105. in Evang. Joann. Est igitur prius Christo donari a Patre, hoc est eligi, quam cognoscere.
